tip: Russian wishes drop into the genitive: сладких снов (sladkikh snov = sweet dreams) literally means of-sweet-dreams.
A feminine direct object takes -у/-ю: интересную книгу (interesnuyu knigu = interesting book), changed from книга (kniga).
Playing a game uses играть (igrat) plus в (v): играет в шахматы (igrayet v shakhmaty = plays chess).
Toasts use за (za) plus the accusative: за ваше здоровье (za vashe zdorovye = to your health).
много (mnogo = many) forces the genitive plural: много туристов (mnogo turistov = many tourists).
Location after в (v) uses the prepositional case: в большом городе (v bolshom gorode = in a big city).
Third person needs свой (svoy) for one's own: свою жену (svoyu zhenu = his own wife); using его (yego) would mean another man's wife.
себя (sebya = oneself) keeps one form for every subject: береги себя (beregi sebya = take care of yourself).
Floors take на (na), not в (v): на пятом этаже (na pyatom etazhe = on the fifth floor).
From five up, the counted noun goes genitive plural: пять тысяч рублей (pyat tysyach rubley = five thousand roubles).
Rain uses the motion verb идёт (idyot = goes): дождь идёт (dozhd idyot = it is raining), literally the rain walks.
Зимой (zimoy = in winter) is instrumental with no preposition; seasons show 'in' by case alone.
Russian time counts toward the next hour: половина десятого (polovina desyatogo = half of the tenth) means 9:30, not 10:30.
